phrases.text: So
welcome back again.
It's time to solve one more problem.
Now, in this problem,
we are given that the motorboat travels at
20 kilometer
per hour
with the current and 12 kilometer per hour
against
the current.
The question is
asking us to find the speed of the boat
in still water.
Let the speed of the boat in still water be b kilometer per hour,
and let the speed of the current be c kilometer per hour. Now, what do these two values mean?
The value b is the speed of the boat when the water is completely still.
That means there is no current in the river.
And c is the speed at which the river water itself is flowing.
Now, let us understand downstream and upstream.
When the boat moves along with the current, the current helps the boat move faster. So downstream speed equals b plus c.
When the boat moves against the current, the current slows the boat down.
So upstream speed equals b minus c.
Now we can use the given values.
Downstream speed,
b plus c equals 20. Upstream speed, b minus c equals 12.
Now this part is done.
If we add both equations,
c gets canceled.
After simplifying, we get 2b equals 32. So b equals 16.
Hence,
the speed of the boat in still water is 16 kilometer per hour. So the correct option is option A.
